waive_sizes.2.2G: Only Windows' RAW codec reads this camera's sensor data, and it refuses a file past 2 GiB: measured 2026-09-23, the same twin decodes at 300 MB and is 'The image is unrecognized' (0x88982F60) at 2.2 GB. The head window cannot stand in: the picture's directories sit past 32 MiB. Under 2 GiB every surface draws it.

Windows' PDF engine (Windows.Data.Pdf) crashes the whole process on a PDF past 2 GiB (measured 2026-09-23: PdfDocument.LoadFromFileAsync on the 2.2 GB twin, from plain PowerShell, none of our code involved), and it is the only PDF renderer here. So a PDF or Illustrator file past 2 GiB is never handed to it (pdf::MAX_ENGINE_BYTES) and keeps its icon.

bay.waive: No real sample exists to grow (corpus-real.json waiver: Casio RAW: absent from raw.pixls.us, rawsamples.ch and every suite searched on 2026-09-17. No sample of any kind).

cal.waive: A CALS raster's header gives no data length: its Group 4 image runs to the end of the file, so a CALS past 256 MiB is a raster of that size, and ImageMagick's CALS reader (the only one) spends its whole 20 s CPU budget on any window of it (measured on the 300 MB twin). The head window skips it (streamsrc/headwin.rs::reads_to_the_end), so it keeps its icon at no cost. Under 256 MiB it renders as before.

k25.waive: A Kodak DC25/DC50 .k25 is a raw that LibRaw identifies partly by its fixed file size: measured, 4 KB of ballast reads the same, 1 MB reads as a different file (256x193, not 256x192). A real .k25 never grows past its fixed size, so no big twin of it can exist.

mdc.waive: LibRaw identifies a Minolta RD-175 .mdc by its exact file size (the header names no camera), so one byte more is already a different file: no bigger twin of it can exist, and no real RD-175 file is bigger than its fixed size.

pix.waive: An Alias/Wavefront .pix is recognised by its runs ending exactly on the last byte (the format has no magic), so no ballast can be added without making it a different file; a genuinely big .pix is just a bigger picture, which the pixel sweep (bigpixels.py) covers.

svg.waive: An SVG is one XML document that has to be parsed whole, and past 256 MiB that is refused on purpose: parsing that much XML inside Explorer costs gigabytes. The only grower that keeps the picture (a long comment) is not how real SVGs get big; embedded images and path data are, and no reader can skip those. Checked at 300 MB: no picture on any surface, as in every release before.
